brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Color-coded category cards with tinted backgrounds create immediate topical legibility and a coherent moody dark palette
File-row craft is strong: consistent type hierarchy, monospace-feeling extension badges, and tidy metadata rows
Spatial scattering hints at proximity-as-meaning, distinguishing it from default file-grid metaphors
dominant_weaknesses: Card placement looks aesthetic-random rather than semantically clustered — proximity carries no readable relational logic between Design/Marketing/Finance
Orphaned floating files (Assets.zip, Demo Video, Quick Note) feel decorative; no visible affordance for grouping, dragging, or linking
Toolbar is generic list-view chrome (Search/View/Filter/Sort) which contradicts the spatial-canvas premise and pulls users back to grid thinking
fix_priorities: Encode real proximity semantics — overlap, connecting lines, or gravity wells — so distance between cards means relatedness
Replace list-style toolbar with canvas-native controls (zoom, cluster, lasso) to reinforce the spatial metaphor
Give orphan files a clear state language (dashed border, magnet-to-cluster hint) instead of identical card styling
Tighten card sizes and reduce empty top half — composition currently leaves a dead zone weakening the canvas feel
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral appeal from colored cards and dark depth, but behavioral clarity is weak because spatial relationships aren't actionable, leaving reflective payoff modest.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially fits — it visually escapes the grid, but proximity is decorative rather than semantic, so the 'spatial canvas by topic' promise is unfulfilled.
